Markov chains

Source: R/stats-stochastic-markov.R
markov_chains.Rd

DiscreteMarkovChain() and ContinuousMarkovChain() of sympy.stats: finite, time homogeneous Markov chains given by a state space and a transition matrix (or a generator matrix for continuous time). A discrete chain is indexed with rv_getitem() (SymPy's Y[t]), a continuous chain is called, C(t). Queries go through P() and E(); pass a transition matrix, a generator matrix or a state space in the given condition with TransitionMatrixOf(), GeneratorMatrixOf() and StochasticStateSpaceOf(), combined with &. Methods such as "communication_classes", "decompose", "canonical_form", "fundamental_matrix", "absorbing_probabilities", "is_regular", "is_ergodic", "is_absorbing_chain", "stationary_distribution", "fixed_row_vector", "limiting_distribution" and "transition_probabilities" are called with rv_attr(). Python tuples come back as lists.

Usage

DiscreteMarkovChain(sym, state_space = NULL, trans_probs = NULL)

ContinuousMarkovChain(sym, state_space = NULL, gen_mat = NULL)

TransitionMatrixOf(process, matrix)

GeneratorMatrixOf(process, matrix)

StochasticStateSpaceOf(process, state_space)

Arguments

sym

The name of the chain.

state_space

Optional state space: a list of states, a Tuple, a FiniteSet or a Range; by default Range(n).

trans_probs

Optional transition matrix (a Matrix or a MatrixSymbol); by default MatrixSymbol("_T", n, n).

gen_mat

Optional generator matrix of a continuous chain.

process

A Markov chain.

matrix

A transition or generator matrix.

Value

A process (an R function), or an assumption to use in a given condition.

Examples

T <- Matrix(list(list(Rational(1, 2), Rational(1, 2)), list(Rational(1, 4), Rational(3, 4))))
Y <- DiscreteMarkovChain("Y", list(0, 1), T)
P(Eq(rv_getitem(Y, 3), 1), Eq(rv_getitem(Y, 1), 0))
#> 5/8
rv_attr(Y, "stationary_distribution")
#> Matrix(1, 2)
#> [1/3, 2/3]
rv_attr(Y, "communication_classes")
#> [[1]]
#> ([0, 1], True, 1) 
#> 
G <- Matrix(list(list(-1, 1), list(1, -1)))
C <- ContinuousMarkovChain("C", list(0, 1), G)
rv_attr(C, "limiting_distribution")
#> Matrix(1, 2)
#> [1/2, 1/2]
